threat_actor: Compromised research process, notebook, extension, or operator token
target_assets: Research data, holdout data, models, credentials, dispatch authority
attack_path: Research process reads secret-bearing values or manipulates artifacts to influence a later deployment
prevention: Run credential visibility guards at research inputs; keep deployment and production trading capabilities separate; gate holdout access
detection: Record denied credential access and holdout use; test wrapper, array, and direct-input boundaries; review artifact provenance
remediation: Isolate the research worker; rotate exposed credentials; invalidate affected artifacts and downstream evidence; audit access history
residual_risk: A shared host or compromised runtime can bypass in-process separation; external process identity and network isolation are unverified

threat_actor: Compromised model publisher, signer, or artifact store
target_assets: Model artifact, trusted keys, prediction and promotion lineage
attack_path: Altered, substituted, or incompatible model is loaded into inference
prevention: Verify Ed25519 signature, artifact digest, schema, and runtime compatibility before inference; bind model identity to promotion authority
detection: Reject invalid signature, hash, schema, or compatibility and record model identity in inference evidence
remediation: Stop inference and promotion; revoke affected trust key; invalidate model descendants; restore a reviewed artifact and re-run gates
residual_risk: Trust-key provisioning, inference service isolation, and signer custody lack independent operational proof

threat_actor: Compromised package maintainer, registry, mirror, or transitive dependency
target_assets: Build runner, source tree, secrets, release artifacts
attack_path: Malicious package code runs during install, test, build, or runtime
prevention: Pin CI dependency versions and restrict installed packages to the declared manifest; review dependency changes
detection: Use CI failures, dependency diffs, package provenance review, and release hygiene as detection points
remediation: Quarantine the package and affected artifacts; rebuild in a clean trusted environment; rotate any exposed credentials
residual_risk: Exact version pins do not authenticate package origin or bytes; no complete hash-locked, signed, or independently attested dependency set exists

threat_actor: Malicious process, compromised host user, log reader, or accidental operator disclosure
target_assets: Production API keys, secrets, credential metadata, runtime process
attack_path: Secret material is exposed through research input, logs, storage, or an unauthorized vault operation
prevention: Use the secret backend; store only fingerprints and metadata in the event ledger; separate configuration from runtime resolution; scan research inputs
detection: Audit allow and deny events; verify the hash chain; test that research and audit payloads exclude secret material
remediation: Revoke and rotate the affected credential; isolate the host; preserve ledger and provider audit evidence; reconcile external access
residual_risk: Host administrators, memory inspection, provider compromise, and production process isolation are outside local test coverage

threat_actor: Compromised operator, stale writer, or unauthorized configuration client
target_assets: Risk limits, venue configuration, model and deployment configuration
attack_path: A changed or stale configuration bypasses expected authority at dispatch or activation
prevention: Bind configuration resolution to durable ID, fingerprint, status, and expiry; require Configuration or Security Admin capability for credential changes
detection: Reject stale, mismatched, revoked, or expired configuration; preserve versioned audit events
remediation: Block dispatch and activation; revoke the bad version; restore an approved version and revalidate dependent gates
residual_risk: Identity issuance, all configuration stores, and hardware-backed immutability are not proven platform-wide

threat_actor: Retrying process, concurrent dispatcher, or ambiguous venue response
target_assets: Order intent, durable dispatch claim, exchange order and resulting position
attack_path: Retry or crash recovery submits the same risk-increasing intent more than once
prevention: Require a persistent side-effect journal and durable intent claim before transport; bind the request fingerprint to its capability
detection: Detect reused IDs, conflicting fingerprints, ambiguous transport outcomes, and venue-versus-ledger divergence
remediation: Stop new dispatch; identify and reconcile venue orders; cancel only by verified identity; repair ledger through an audited recovery
residual_risk: Venue-side exactly-once behavior and real exchange reconciliation are not verified

threat_actor: Malicious client, stale queue, duplicated message, or restored old process
target_assets: Order authority, decision TTL, idempotency state, event stream
attack_path: A valid prior request or authority is replayed after use, expiry, or state change
prevention: Bind requests to idempotency fingerprints, causal dependencies, validity windows, and one-shot capabilities
detection: Reject expired or consumed authority and conflicting ID reuse; compare ledger sequence and current dependency state
remediation: Block the affected path; revoke or invalidate authority; reconcile pending side effects and downstream records before resuming
residual_risk: External transport replay and venue nonce guarantees have not been independently assessed

threat_actor: Compromised deployment identity, research role, CI token, or promotion client
target_assets: Model release, deployment state, production endpoint and risk allocation
attack_path: A caller activates a model or environment without required promotion, compatibility, approval, or deployment authority
prevention: Separate Deployment capability; require durable promotion and one-shot activation authority with exact environment and artifact binding
detection: Reject missing, expired, reused, or mismatched authority; audit promotion and activation state
remediation: Disable activation authority; halt or roll back through the verified runbook; preserve events and repeat required gates
residual_risk: Trusted identity assignment and independent approval are absent; provider-side enforcement is not verified

threat_actor: Compromised host administrator, storage operator, or privileged application process
target_assets: Append-only event ledger, evidence history, incident and approval records
attack_path: An actor alters, truncates, reorders, or suppresses audit events
prevention: Use a hash-chained durable event store; bind writes to stable event IDs; keep secrets out of the ledger
detection: Verify the event hash chain at protected boundaries; detect conflicting event IDs, missing records, and replay divergence
remediation: Freeze dependent decisions; preserve a forensic copy; restore only from a separately verified backup; reconcile before reopening actions
residual_risk: Local hash chains do not prevent privileged storage rewrite; independent immutable retention, access monitoring, and backup recovery are unverified

threat_actor: Compromised source host, maintainer account, build action, signing key, or artifact channel
target_assets: Repository source, CI workflow, release artifacts, signing and verification keys
attack_path: Attacker substitutes source, workflow action, model artifact, or release metadata
prevention: Pin CI actions and dependencies where configured; verify signed model artifacts; restrict trusted-key and release changes to reviewed policy
detection: Compare source and artifact hashes; review protected-branch events, workflow provenance, signatures, and release manifests
remediation: Revoke compromised keys and tokens; stop releases; quarantine artifacts; rebuild from a reviewed commit and revalidate provenance
residual_risk: Complete source-to-build provenance, action/dependency attestations, signer custody, and independent repository review are not established
